## What it does

`importtextfiles` reads every file in a directory matching a file pattern, sorted by name, and stores each file as one observation with two `strL` variables: the file name and the complete file contents. Contents are written directly from Mata, so no intermediate file is created and embedded quotes, newlines, and arbitrary bytes are preserved exactly.

It is built for corpora of documents — transcripts, notes, model outputs — that need to sit alongside structured data in Stata. Because `strL` variables hold real newline characters, no placeholder such as a literal `\n` is needed: exporting with `export delimited` or reading the `.dta` with `pandas.read_stata` yields the text with proper line breaks.

## Installation

From GitHub:

```stata
net install importtextfiles, from("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steffenerickson/importtextfiles/main/") replace
```

Requirements: Stata 17 or later. No dependencies outside official Stata.

## Quick start

Read a folder of `.txt` transcripts into memory, normalizing line endings:

```stata
importtextfiles using "raw/2023-24 Transcripts", clear normalize
```

Load a second corpus into its own frame without touching the current data, or read Markdown notes as single-line cells:

```stata
importtextfiles using "raw/2024-25 Transcripts", frame(t2) normalize
importtextfiles using "notes", pattern(*.md) separator(" ") clear
```

## Main features

### Exact contents, no temporary files

Each file is read and written to the dataset from Mata, so quotes, embedded newlines, and arbitrary bytes arrive unchanged. Without options, bytes are stored exactly as found on disk.

### Line-ending control

The `normalize` option converts Windows (CRLF) and old-Mac (CR) line endings to LF and strips trailing newlines — recommended when the data will be read by Python or R. The `separator()` option goes further and joins lines with any string (for example a single space) to produce single-line cells.

### Frames and safe overwriting

With `frame()`, the dataset is created in a new frame and the current frame and its data are left untouched. The `clear` option is required only when data in memory (or an existing frame of the same name) would be discarded; otherwise the command exits with an error rather than overwriting.

### Stored results

The command returns the number of files read in `r(N)`, along with the directory, pattern, frame, and variable names used, so downstream code can check and log what was imported.

## Syntax reference

Full syntax and options are in the help file (`help importtextfiles`) shipped with the package.
